summary: compactOfflineFields (internal/cli/offline.go) is compactFields' offline-scoped counterpart: it applies the same verbose-field blocklist recursively at every nesting level, not just the top level, plus two Peloton-specific bulky field names (achievement_templates, muscle_group_score) confirmed present in real workout_details payloads. offline output routinely wraps the real payload under a structural key (detail/history on offline_workout, result on any offline command that returns a caveat) rather than exposing fields at the top level, so the shared compactFields (helpers.go, unchanged, still used by every live single-fetch command) left --compact doing nothing for these shapes -- the wrapper keys themselves never matched the blocklist. Deliberately scoped to printOffline only: live commands' flat responses don't have this wrapping problem, and their nested objects (e.g. workouts show's "ride" object) are meaningful content --compact should leave intact, not blindly recurse into. Any future regen must keep printOffline calling compactOfflineFields (not compactFields) for --compact.
reason: NEW ISSUE C from a fourth live post-fix verification sweep: --compact's own help text promises "only key fields (id, name, status, timestamps)" but for offline_workout returned the complete, unstripped detail+history payload -- achievement_templates, muscle_group_score, and the full nested "ride" object all survived, since compactObjectFields (the shared single-object path) is a shallow, top-level-only blocklist and the wrapper keys ("detail"/"history") never matched it. Presented three options to the user (recurse into offline's wrapper shapes / fix the documentation instead / redesign --compact broadly for all single objects); user chose the recommended scoped-recursion option.
validated_outcome: go build/vet/test/govulncheck and verify_skill.py all green.
